column1: # Ghent PDF Output Suite 5.0 — the expected-results table.
# INTERNAL REGRESSION EVIDENCE ONLY. Passing the gate that reads this table is
# not a Ghent Workgroup conformance certification; that programme has its own
# process and this product is not in it. Nothing derived from this file may be
# worded as certified.
# Every `expected` cell is PARAPHRASED from the suite's own per-patch ReadMe —
# the documentation that ships inside the archive, never a reading of what this
# product happens to produce and never Ghostscript or pdf.js as an oracle. The
# corpus itself is gitignored (scripts/fetch-ghent-suite.py); this table, the
# script and the manifest are what the repository carries.
# The suite's own verdict is VISUAL — a clear X, or a patch that stops matching
# the reference image beside it. No reference RIP exists here, so a machine
# cannot pronounce that verdict, and the table does not pretend otherwise:
# `checks` are the machine-decidable preconditions the app's own surfaces must
# report for the visual verdict to be reachable at all (the plate set, the ink
# inventory, the overprint state, the colour family, the image construct, the
# output intent). A row whose preconditions fail cannot render correctly; a row
# whose preconditions pass has been shown only that much. The human half is the
# assembled pages beside their reference page.
# status: `applicable` or `not_applicable`. A not_applicable row is excluded
# from the pass tally and carries the patch's own documented reason — it is
# never silently green.
# checks tokens, each backed by a function in tests/test_ghent_output.py:
#   inks:A|B        list_inks names exactly these spot colorants
#   family:F        list_inks reports colour family F on the page
#   overprint       list_overprint finds at least one overprinting paint
#   opm:N           an /ExtGState in the file declares that overprint mode
#   ocgs            list_layers reports optional-content groups
#   filter:F        an image XObject uses that decode filter
#   bpc16           an image XObject carries 16 bits per component
#   outputintent    the file declares an output intent with an embedded profile
